description: Natural Hazards Research Summit 2022: Design for Tornadoes: How a Disaster and a Decade of R&D Led to the First-Ever Tornado Load Requirements in Building Codes and Standards is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Marc Levitan, National Institute of Standards and Technology (nist.gov). This poster gives an overview of how the devastating 2011 Joplin, MO tornado initiated a decade of R&D recently culminating in tornado load requirements being developed and adopted into the ASCE 7 Standard and the International Building Code. Coverage: Joplin, MO. DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-xxfy-ge39. Keywords: Tornadoes, Tornado Load Methodology, Hazard Maps, Joplin, Codes & Standards, Economic Analysis. Published 2023-03-10. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
